active_paradigms.idea: Globally optimize all 11 barycentric point locations with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution, without forcing the three container vertices to be selected.
active_paradigms.description: The current constructor fixes three of the eleven points at the container vertices, then anneals only eight points and finally uses an SLSQP polish within one fixed orientation-sign cell. This is fast enough to find a reasonable basin, but the vertex assumption removes six continuous degrees of freedom and is not implied by the evaluator. Represent every point by two bounded variables transformed into the closed barycentric simplex, for example use (r,s) in [0,1]^2 and map to u=r*(1-s), v=s, or use a sorted-stick transformation. Define the objective directly as the negative of the evaluator's normalized minimum determinant over all 165 triples; do not optimize the current low-area surrogate, because ranking changes among the lowest constraints can matter substantially. Call differential_evolution once on all 22 variables with a fixed seed, Sobol initialization, sufficiently large population, mutation dithering, and polishing enabled only if the final point remains valid. Remove translational/symmetry redundancy by fixing one selected point to a canonical chamber only if this does not force it to be a container vertex; alternatively evaluate reflected/permuted equivalents internally in the objective. This population method can cross collinearity and orientation-chart boundaries that the current signed SLSQP formulation cannot cross. Return the best feasible member explicitly reprojected into barycentric coordinates, and recompute all 165 areas before returning it.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized. The main expected gain is recovering arrangements whose optimal active geometry does not include all three enclosing vertices and escaping the incumbent's fixed sign chart; execution time is secondary but should be bounded by maxiter and popsize.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use the exact absolute determinant normalization used by the evaluator, not Euclidean area with an inconsistent factor. A simple clipped coordinate map can create many boundary duplicates, so prefer a smooth square-to-simplex map. Differential evolution in 22 dimensions needs an explicit evaluation budget and vectorized determinant calculation; avoid nested Python loops. Never accept a candidate merely because its penalized objective is good: reconstruct Cartesian coordinates and run an exact inside-triangle and minimum-area check before returning.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.shgo as a deterministic global feasible-region search on a symmetry-reduced, active-constraint epigraph formulation.
active_paradigms.description: The current approach treats the objective as a noisy minimum and uses stochastic moves, followed by a local solver whose orientation signs are frozen from one incumbent. Instead formulate the true maximin problem with a scalar t and constraints |det(i,j,k)| >= t for all triples, after imposing a canonical ordering/symmetry convention that removes equivalent rotations and reflections of the enclosing equilateral triangle. For each plausible orientation chamber, encode signed determinants det_sign*det >= t and barycentric simplex inequalities, then use scipy.optimize.shgo directly on that chamber's epigraph objective -t. SHGO's simplicial sampling is deterministic and is specifically useful when a local optimizer repeatedly finds different nonsmooth basins. The important structural change is to optimize all eleven points, not just eight, while using geometric symmetry only to choose one equivalent representative rather than assuming vertices are occupied. Begin with chambers inferred from combinatorial orderings of a high-quality known layout, because solving every possible orientation assignment is intractable. A feasible SHGO solution identifies an active set of nearly equal determinant constraints, which is much more informative than the annealer's broad low-area merit reward. Compare every returned candidate with exact absolute areas, since only that final calculation defines the score.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized through a true epigraph variable and deterministic exploration of alternative orientation cells. This specifically addresses the current SLSQP polish being unable to improve after a beneficial determinant would need to change sign.
active_paradigms.cautions: Absolute-area constraints cannot be submitted to one smooth local chart without choosing signs; a chamber must be internally consistent and candidates crossing a zero determinant must be rejected. Full 22-dimensional SHGO is expensive, so symmetry reduction and a compact set of geometrically motivated chambers are essential. Do not claim t is valid solely from solver feasibility tolerance; lower it slightly or verify all 165 absolute determinants exactly before output. Ensure canonical ordering constraints do not accidentally exclude the optimum rather than merely select among symmetry-equivalent copies.

active_paradigms.idea: Apply scipy.optimize.dual_annealing directly to a smooth bottleneck surrogate with continuation-free log-sum-exp, while retaining all 11 points as variables.
active_paradigms.description: The existing annealer moves one point at a time, selects that point from currently critical triples, and scores a hand-tuned minimum-plus-nearby-mean merit. Its local moves can be effective, but this merit is not the evaluator objective and its hand-selected temperatures, restart count, and vertex fixation can trap the search below the benchmark. Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing once over a full barycentric parameterization of all 11 points, with a deterministic seed and finite bounds. Replace the discontinuous minimum during search by a numerically stable soft-min of the 165 normalized absolute determinants, using a fixed high inverse-temperature chosen so that only the genuinely limiting triangles receive material weight. Unlike the present merit, this gives every constraint a differentiable influence and prevents a solution that improves the first area while silently collapsing another nearly active one. The dual annealing visiting distribution can make coordinated changes in many points, which are often necessary when the bottleneck triangles form an interdependent active network. At the end, choose the best sampled state according to the exact hard minimum, not according to the surrogate, and map it exactly into the container. This is a distinct stochastic global-search regime from custom one-coordinate Metropolis moves and does not require the orientation signs used by the current final polish.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized, with the surrogate used only to make the search landscape less brittle. Favor exact-minimum incumbent tracking throughout so the final combined_score, rather than surrogate quality, determines the returned arrangement.
active_paradigms.cautions: Compute soft-min with the shifted log-sum-exp formula to avoid overflow at high inverse-temperature. A surrogate can overvalue a configuration with many moderately small triangles, so retain a separate exact minimum incumbent after every objective evaluation. The square-to-simplex transform must cover boundary points, since optimal arrangements may place some points on edges. Set maxfun conservatively because each objective evaluation involves all 165 triples, and do not add a second polishing stage if strict single-call construction is required.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace runtime annealing with a cached certified 11-point construction returned by numpy.array
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a fixed-seed, coordinate-wise simulated annealer in barycentric coordinates: it fixes all three container vertices, optimizes the other eight points, and scores a smoothed lower-tail merit before a greedy maximin polish. Its strengths are exact feasibility by construction, cached updates of only the 45 incident triples, and direct use of the normalized determinant that the evaluator measures. Its main limitation is that 448,000 stochastic local moves are spent rediscovering one basin on every evaluation, while the final returned state remains far below the supplied benchmark. Search offline for a strong 11-point certificate once, preferably using the known symmetry class and all 165 evaluator determinants, then paste its 22 decimal coordinates into the constructor. At evaluation time, make the function consist solely of `np.array(precomputed_points, dtype=float)`; no random generator, optimization, or imports beyond NumPy are needed. Preserve more than 10 significant decimal digits and verify the exact evaluator formula locally before embedding the constants. This is structurally different from improving the online search: it converts the task into deterministic certificate delivery, giving negligible evaluation time and eliminating run-to-run basin risk.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary normalized minimum area first; use the benchmark 0.036529889880030156 as a target and retain a small numerical safety margin so coordinate rounding does not reduce the active minimum. Evaluation time becomes essentially zero.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not round a certificate aggressively, and do not place nominal boundary points infinitesimally outside the three checked half-planes. The evaluator uses all triples of returned points only, not the container vertices unless they are explicitly returned. A candidate whose displayed score is exactly the benchmark can lose from floating-point rounding, so embed a verified interior-safe or higher-precision realization.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.minimize with SLSQP on a signed-determinant epigraph formulation
tried_paradigms.description: Use one direct `scipy.optimize.minimize(..., method='SLSQP')` call to solve for all point coordinates and an epigraph variable t. Parameterize every movable point by barycentric coordinates `(u,v)`, with inequalities `u >= 0`, `v >= 0`, and `1-u-v >= 0`; optionally keep only the three proven container-corner points fixed if that structural hypothesis is verified. For a selected orientation sign s for each triple, impose the smooth nonlinear constraint `s * det_ijk(u,v) - t >= 0` for all 165 triples and maximize t. Obtain the sign chart from one fixed good incumbent or from the intended certificate family, because within a nondegenerate basin each absolute determinant has a constant sign. This directly attacks the evaluator’s true bottleneck rather than the current code’s minimum-plus-tail surrogate, and it moves all coordinates jointly rather than one point at a time. Initialize with a fixed incumbent and set tight `ftol`, large `maxiter`, and analytic determinant Jacobians if practical. If successful, the returned t is exactly the normalized evaluator minimum because affine barycentric determinants equal the enclosing-area-normalized triangle areas.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Maximize the epigraph variable t, which is the exact `min_area_normalized`; the secondary benefit is a much shorter deterministic call than 20 annealing restarts.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The sign pattern is essential: blindly constraining every determinant to one orientation excludes valid configurations. Check after the solve that no determinant changed sign and recompute `min(abs(det))` independently, since SLSQP’s reported objective alone is not a certificate. SLSQP is local, so this is best as a high-precision basin solver from a fixed strong layout, not as a replacement for global discovery.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution directly on a feasibility-preserving transformed maximin objective
tried_paradigms.description: Use a single `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` call as a global direct solver, replacing the current custom annealer and its hand-tuned merit schedule. Let each of the eight nonvertex points have two variables `(r,q)` in `[0,1]^2` and map them to barycentric coordinates by `u=r` and `v=(1-r)q`, which guarantees `u,v >= 0` and `u+v <= 1` without penalties or repair projections. For each population member, assemble the 11 points, vectorize all 165 absolute normalized determinants, and return the negative of their minimum as the objective. Seed the solver with a fixed integer, use a reasonably large population, mutation dithering, and `polish=False` so the implementation remains one global library call rather than a hidden local-search pipeline. Supply a fixed high-quality `x0` encoding of the current best or a known structured layout, while allowing the population to escape its basin. This tackles the principal weakness of the current approach—coordinate-wise local moves and a surrogate objective—because candidate layouts are evolved globally using the exact objective. Once a strong result is found, it should be frozen as literal coordinates under the first idea rather than rerun during normal evaluation.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact negative minimum of all 165 normalized areas, with global-basin discovery prioritized over evaluation time during offline construction.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Differential evolution in 16 dimensions can be expensive, so it is primarily an offline certificate-discovery tool, not a desirable final submitted constructor. Do not use an additive infeasibility penalty: the `(r,q)` transformation is important because penalties distort the already nonsmooth maximin landscape. Ensure that the objective does not accidentally include container vertices unless they are part of the 11 returned points, and always recompute the evaluator score from the final transformed coordinates.
